tutorial.title: Understanding Python Packages
tutorial.descriptionContent: Group modules in packages, compare import styles, and learn where Python finds modules from different sources.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who can create and import custom modules.

lessons.title: Prepare the package
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've already used modules: A module is just a Python file that we expose for us or others to use.

A package is a directory containing one or more modules.

lessons.title: Expose the first module
lessons.interactiveContent:
In __init__.py, the period means this package. Complete the first module that order_tools exposes.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In __init__.py, the period means this package. Expose the module that formats a total, using a relative import.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Expose another module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add validation to the same relative import. This makes both modules part of the package's public surface.

Make sure to pick validation.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add validation to the same relative import. This makes both modules part of the package's public surface.

Make sure to pick ., followed by validation.

lessons.title: Import the package
lessons.interactiveContent:
Now __init__.py exposes both modules, so import order_tools loads that public surface. Complete the package name.

Make sure to pick order_tools.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Now __init__.py exposes both modules, so import order_tools loads them. Complete the names to validate and format the total.

Make sure to pick order_tools, followed by validation, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Import selected modules
lessons.interactiveContent:
To use a module as a direct name, list it in a from import. This avoids the order_tools. prefix. Complete the first name.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To use a module as a direct name, list it in a from import. This avoids the order_tools. prefix. Complete the first name.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Use selected modules
lessons.interactiveContent:
Specifying validation in the from import makes it a direct name in script.py. Complete its call.

Make sure to pick validation.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Specifying validation in the from import makes it a direct name in script.py. Complete its call.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally validation.

lessons.title: Import a hidden module
lessons.interactiveContent:
If __init__.py doesn't expose a module, import its full dotted path instead. Complete the first module name.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If __init__.py doesn't expose a module, import its full dotted path instead. Complete the import and the formatting call.

Make sure to pick import, followed by formatting, and finally format_total.

lessons.title: Spot the module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which item is a module inside the order_tools package?

formatting.pyorder_tools

Make sure to pick formatting.py.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You add discount.py beside formatting.py. Which pair names the package and your new module?

Package: order_tools; module: discount.pyPackage: discount.py; module: order_toolsPackage: script.py; module: discount.py

Package: order_tools; module: discount.py.

lessons.title: Find the public surface
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which file chooses the modules exposed by the order_tools package?

__init__.pyscript.py

Make sure to pick __init__.py.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You want import order_tools to expose only validation. Which file and import should you change?

In __init__.py: from . import validationIn script.py: from order_tools import validationIn validation.py: from . import formatting

In __init__.py: from . import validation.

lessons.title: Trace a new package
lessons.interactiveContent:
shipping_tools/__init__.py exposes rates and labels. Complete the package-only import.

Make sure to pick shipping_tools.
lessons.hardModeContent:
shipping_tools/__init__.py exposes rates and labels. Complete the package-only import.

Make sure to pick import, followed by shipping_tools, and finally weight.

lessons.title: Choose an import style
lessons.interactiveContent:
The same order_tools package supports several import styles. Each style changes the names available in script.py, not the package files.

Make sure to pick order_tools.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The same order_tools package supports several import styles. Each style changes the names available in script.py, not the package files.

Make sure to pick import, followed by order_tools, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Keep the package name
lessons.interactiveContent:
import order_tools keeps the package name. Reach format_total() through the package and module names.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
import order_tools keeps the package name. Reach format_total() through the package and module names.

Make sure to pick order_tools, followed by formatting.

lessons.title: Import the submodule
lessons.interactiveContent:
You can import a submodule with its full dotted path. The call still starts with order_tools.formatting.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import the submodule containing format_total() by its full dotted path. The call still starts with order_tools.formatting.

Make sure to pick import, followed by order_tools, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Import the module name
lessons.interactiveContent:
from order_tools import formatting brings formatting into script.py. Complete the imported module name.

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A from import brings a module into script.py directly. Import the module so the shown call needs no package prefix.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally formatting.

lessons.title: Use the module name
lessons.interactiveContent:
A selected-module import removes the package prefix from later calls. Complete the module name before format_total().

Make sure to pick formatting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A selected-module import removes the package prefix from later calls. Complete the module name before format_total().

Make sure to pick import, followed by formatting.

lessons.title: Import the function
lessons.interactiveContent:
A direct import brings only format_total() into script.py. Complete the function name in the import.

Make sure to pick format_total.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A direct import brings only format_total() into script.py. Complete the function name in the import.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally format_total.

lessons.title: Use an alias
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use as to give the imported module a shorter local name. The package files keep their original names.

Make sure to pick fmt.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use as to give the imported module a shorter local name. The package files keep their original names.

Make sure to pick formatting, followed by as, and finally fmt.

lessons.title: Choose the package style
lessons.interactiveContent:
script.py keeps the full order_tools.formatting call. Which import style does it use?

Package-only importSelected-module import

Package-only import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
script.py keeps the full order_tools.formatting call. Which import style does it use?

Package-only importDirect function import

Make sure to pick Package-only import.

lessons.title: Choose a shorter name
lessons.interactiveContent:
Import formatting as fmt, then use that alias to format a different total.

Make sure to pick fmt.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import formatting as fmt, then use that alias to format a different total.

Make sure to pick from, followed by import, and finally fmt.

lessons.title: Import one name
lessons.interactiveContent:
Import only is_valid_total() from the validation module. Complete the function name in the import.

Make sure to pick is_valid_total.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import only is_valid_total() from the validation module. Complete the function name in the import.

Make sure to pick from, followed by validation, and finally is_valid_total.

lessons.title: Modules have authors
lessons.interactiveContent:
Modules can be written by your company, Python's developers, or another company. Assume Python can find all three.

No matter who wrote one, the same import keyword can load it.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Modules can be written by your company, Python's developers, or another company. Assume Python can find all three.

No matter who wrote one, the same import keyword can load it.

Load math, then company_tools, then text_formatting.

Make sure to pick import, followed by math, and finally company_tools.

lessons.title: Import an internal module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Your company created company_tools for internal projects. The project contains the module file.

Import it, then use its function to format a total.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your company created company_tools for internal projects. The project contains the module file.

Import it, then use its function to format a total.

Make sure to pick import, followed by company_tools, and finally format_total.

lessons.title: Import a Python module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Python's developers include math in the standard library. Import it, then use its function to find a square root.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Python's developers include math in the standard library. Its sqrt() function finds a square root.

Import the module and use that function to find the square root of 25.

Make sure to pick import, followed by math, and finally sqrt.

lessons.title: Import a shared function
lessons.interactiveContent:
Another company shared text_formatting. The active environment contains the installed module.

Type from to import its function, then use the function directly.

Make sure to type from.

lessons.title: Find project and Python modules
lessons.interactiveContent:
Python can find a module file in the current project. Here, company_tools.py provides company_tools.

Python finds math somewhere else: in the standard library that comes with Python.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Python can find a module file in the current project. Here, company_tools.py provides company_tools.

Python finds math somewhere else: in the standard library that comes with Python.

Make sure to pick import, followed by company_tools, and finally math.

lessons.title: Find installed modules
lessons.interactiveContent:
A shared module can live outside the project and Python's standard library.

Once it is installed in the active Python environment, Python can find and import it.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A shared module can live outside the project and Python's standard library.

Once it is installed in the active Python environment, Python can find and import it.

Import the installed module text_formatting so you can use its module name.

Make sure to pick import, followed by text_formatting.

lessons.title: Sources stay outside imports
lessons.interactiveContent:
An import statement names code Python can find. It doesn't say who wrote the module or where it came from.

Assume Python can find all three. Complete the keyword that works for every source.

Make sure to pick import.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An import statement names code Python can find. It doesn't say who wrote the module or where it came from.

Assume Python can find all three. Complete the keyword that works for every source, and import company_tools before text_formatting.

Make sure to pick import, followed by company_tools, and finally text_formatting.

lessons.title: Use the same dotted rule
lessons.interactiveContent:
With import, keep the module name before the dot. This works the same way for every source.

All three modules are available. Complete the final import keyword.

Make sure to pick text_formatting, followed by .clean_text.
lessons.hardModeContent:
With import, keep the module name before the dot. This works the same way for every source.

All three modules are available. Complete the final import keyword.

Make sure to pick import, followed by math, text_formatting, and finally clean_text.

lessons.title: Use the same from import
lessons.interactiveContent:
With from, select one name and use it directly. This also works for every module source.

All three modules are available. Complete the final from import.

Make sure to pick from.
lessons.hardModeContent:
With from, select one name and use it directly. This also works for every module source.

All three modules are available. Complete the final from import.

Make sure to pick from, followed by math, and finally import.

lessons.title: Choose import syntax
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which statement imports the entire internal module so the code can use company_tools.format_total(25)?

import company_toolsfrom company_tools import format_total

import company_tools.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which statement imports the entire internal module so the code can use company_tools.format_total(25)?

import company_toolsfrom company_tools import format_total as company_toolsfrom company_tools import format_total

Make sure to pick import company_tools.

lessons.title: Choose from import syntax
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which statement imports sqrt from Python's math module so the code can call sqrt(25) directly?

from math import sqrtimport math

from math import sqrt.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which statement imports sqrt from Python's math module so the code can call sqrt(25) directly?

from math import sqrtfrom math import math.sqrt

Make sure to pick from math import sqrt.

lessons.title: One rule for every source
lessons.interactiveContent:
A module can come from the project, Python's standard library, or the active environment. What must be true before an import works?

Python can find the module in one of those placesThe import statement names who created the module

Python can find the module in one of those places.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You move a module out of the project and install it in the active Python environment. Python can find it there. What changes?

The same import statement can still load it.You must change import to from because it is installed.You must add the module author to the import statement.

The same import statement can still load it.
